_readme: Bibliographic details for the works Midad imports into Zotero.
The repositories carry no imprint, so these are researched best-guesses for
convenience ONLY. A work exists in many editions; unless 'verified' is true,
check the details against the copy you actually used before citing.
Keyed by the work key shown in the collection MOC / the SourceWork key
(<collection>:<id>). Any field here overrides the derived value; omit a key
to fall back to the repository/source name.
Fields: title, publisher, place, date, edition, translators[], authors[],
editors[], note, verified (true = checked against the physical/authoritative edition).
A name is normally a string; the last word becomes Zotero's last name. For names
the split gets wrong (compound surnames like 'Abdel Haleem'), use an object:
{ "first": "M. A. S.", "last": "Abdel Haleem" }  — or { "name": "…" } for a
single-field name. This override is used for the Zotero creator and the YAML link.

dictionary:lanelexicon.edition: 8 vols. An Arabic-English Lexicon, derived from the best and the most copious Eastern sources
dictionary:lanelexicon.note: Lane's great-nephew Stanley Lane-Poole completed vols. VI-VIII and compiled the Supplement (Book II, 1877-1893) from Lane's notes; the work was issued in two books, the second being the Supplement. The digitised text here is the Perseus Digital Library's, via laneslexicon/LexiconDatabase, and that database folds the Supplement into the Lexicon as one work: its rows are a suffix block in the scan's own numbering, from id 49,881 on — 3,034 of the 52,914 rows, 609 of them roots — attached under the corresponding Lexicon roots. A root note marks where they begin with a '## Supplement' heading. The Lexicon's own cross-references to it survive in the text ('see Supplement' at ك، ل، ه، هبر، كرز، مزر، نسناس).
